title: LLV-GBR200: two-entry tables improve quadratic-space low-source time

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2N), the single LLV-GBR200 algorithm in proof.md recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY branch charged work is O(2^((1/2)sqrt(n)log2(n)+2sqrt(n)(log2(n))^(1/4))), with an absolute outside constant and exact growth index1/2. For n>=2^4096 use v=floor(sqrt n),r=ceil(sqrt n),ell=ceil(log2n),ell2=ceil(log2ell),D=ell+2ell2+4,m=floor((v-256ell)/D),kappa=ceil(log2(m+2))+3,lambda=1,A_bar=ceil((n+m*kappa)/m)+2,center=ceil(ell*(m-1)/2),fan_i=A_bar+ell*i-center. Exact quadratic prefixes choose full widths fan_i-1-kappa and one final k=R+kappa+1-input merge with widthR and one-qubit output, including R=0. Dbar=2K*fan_max*A_bar^m,Dcap=2^12nDbar,Ccap=2^13nDbar. Section14 uses disjoint consumed-leaf counts, bounds every level by an affine expression with negative slope, and proves log2T<=sqrt(n)log2(n)/2+sqrt(n)log2log2(n)+O(sqrt n)+O((log n)^2), which fits the exact supported envelope. Serial lookup/list exclusion, source/LE, generation, arithmetic, failed work and cleanup are all charged jointly with all other claims.

For this same LLV-GBR200 configuration, every N,s and EVERY branch, peak classical space is O(n^2) bits with an absolute constant and exact growth index0. There are O(n) retained phase tables, each containing two 3n-bit labels. The single current tuple list uses O(n) bits; current residue/sort/input arrays use O(n^(3/2)log n)<=O(n^2). The stack, cap and parameter arithmetic, source/LE scratch, streamed gate/address generation and decoder records/candidate arithmetic fit O(n^2), as detailed in Section14. No exponential circuit, full tree or truth table is stored. This holds jointly with unconditional full-secret success and all other claims.

For this same LLV-GBR200 configuration, every N,s and EVERY branch, peak quantum allocation is O(n) qubits with an absolute constant and exact growth index0. Pending siblings use O(sum_i fan_i)=O(n); current finish/search uses O(fan_max)=O(sqrt(n)log n)<=O(n) scratch, reset and reused between trials. Source/LE, rank/projection, failed work and cleanup are included. The exact centered sum gives m*A_bar<=n+m*kappa+3m. This holds jointly with unconditional full-secret success and all other claims.

For this same LLV-GBR200 configuration, every N,s and EVERY branch, all fresh acquired copies number O(2^((1/2)sqrt n)), with an absolute constant and exact growth index1/2. Rejected, discarded, failed and aborted acquisitions all count. Dbar=2K*fan_max*A_bar^m,Dcap=2^12nDbar,Ccap=2^13nDbar. AM-GM bounds the full fan-in product by A_bar^m; all prefixes and final arities are covered by fan_max*A_bar^m. Section8 proves A_bar<=fan_max<=2sqrt(n)*ell and mlog2A_bar<=mD/2<=(v-256ell)/2, giving the literal nCcap+K<=2^(v/2). Tail R=0 uses k=kappa+1, correctly included. The finite branch changes only outside constants. This holds jointly with unconditional full-secret success and all other claims.

For the same LLV-GBR200 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
